name: Flight 4
summary: Flight 4 was the first flight in which both stages returned for controlled ocean landings. Booster 11 lost one engine on ascent and lit 12 of 13 engines for its landing burn, then made a soft splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 7.5 minutes after launch. Ship 29 kept attitude control through reentry despite visible flap damage and lost tiles, then performed a landing flip and burn and splashed down in the Indian Ocean about 66 minutes after launch, roughly 6 km from its target according to Elon Musk.
highlights: First soft splashdown of a Super Heavy booster
Ship flap visibly damaged during reentry but stayed controllable
First ship landing flip and burn into the ocean
Ship landed about 6 km from target

objectives.label: Booster landing burn to a virtual tower over the Gulf
Ship controlled splashdown in the Indian Ocean

boosterFate: Soft splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico at T+7:24; tipped over and broke apart in the water.
shipFate: Controlled splashdown in the Indian Ocean at T+1:05:56.

sources.title: Starship finds success on fourth flight test
